questions.text: Quick Revision - Ecosystem and Food Chain

definitionBean.title: Ecosystem and Food Chain
definitionBean.definition: A system formed by the interaction of biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) components is called an 'Ecosystem'; and the feeding relationships among organisms are called a 'Food Chain'[cite: 15].
definitionBean.explanation: Energy flow in a food chain is always unidirectional, and only 10% of energy at each trophic level is transferred to the next level (Lindeman's 10% Law)[cite: 15].
importantPoints: Components of ecosystem: Biotic (producers, consumers, decomposers) and Abiotic (temperature, light, soil)[cite: 15]
Food chain: Producer $\rightarrow$ Primary consumer $\rightarrow$ Secondary consumer[cite: 15]
10% Energy Law: Transfer of only 10% energy from one trophic level to the next[cite: 15]
Biological Magnification: Progressive increase in the concentration of harmful chemicals[cite: 15]

questions.text: Quick Revision - Ozone Layer and Waste Management

definitionBean.title: Ozone Layer and Waste Management
definitionBean.definition: The ozone ($\text{O}_3$) layer found in the upper atmosphere protects the Earth from harmful ultraviolet (UV) rays of the sun; and waste management involves classifying substances as biodegradable and non-biodegradable[cite: 15].
definitionBean.explanation: The ozone layer is depleting due to gases like CFCs (Chlorofluorocarbons)[cite: 15]. Substances decomposed by microorganisms are biodegradable, while those that do not decompose are non-biodegradable[cite: 15].
importantPoints: Main cause of ozone depletion: CFC (Chlorofluorocarbon) gas[cite: 15]

parts.statement: What is an ecosystem? Give an example of an artificial ecosystem[cite: 15].
parts.correct_answer: System of living and abiotic components is ecosystem; Example: Aquarium[cite: 15].
parts.explanation: All the living organisms and abiotic components of an area together form an ecosystem[cite: 15]. An aquarium or a garden is an example of an artificial ecosystem[cite: 15].

parts.statement: What is the difference between a food chain and a food web? Why is energy flow unidirectional[cite: 15]?
parts.correct_answer: Food chain is linear while food web is a complex network[cite: 15].
parts.explanation: A food chain is a straight-line sequence of organisms, whereas a food web is a complex network of multiple interconnected food chains[cite: 15]. Energy flow is unidirectional because the energy transferred from one trophic level to the next does not return and is lost as heat[cite: 15].

questions.text: Subject: Ozone Layer and Waste Management

parts.statement: What is the ozone layer? Why is it important for us? Write the main cause of its depletion[cite: 15].
parts.correct_answer: Ozone protects from UV rays; depletion is caused by CFC gas[cite: 15].
parts.explanation: Ozone ($\text{O}_3$) is a layer formed by three atoms of oxygen found in the stratosphere[cite: 15]. It prevents harmful ultraviolet (UV) rays coming from the sun from reaching the Earth, preventing diseases like skin cancer[cite: 15]. Its main cause of depletion is CFC (chlorofluorocarbon) gas used in refrigerators and ACs[cite: 15].

parts.statement: Write the difference between biodegradable and non-biodegradable substances. Give one example of each[cite: 15].
parts.explanation: Biodegradable substances are broken down into simple substances by microorganisms (e.g., vegetable peels); whereas non-biodegradable substances are not naturally decomposed and persist in the environment for a long time (e.g., plastic)[cite: 15].
